title: Why I Changed My Mind About the Millennium
author: Sam Storms
summary: Storms recounts his move from dispensational premillennialism (via popular prophecy books) to amillennialism, explaining the exegetical reasons that persuaded him.
note: Existence and author confirmed via search index; the page itself could not be fetched from the research environment.

title: Amillennialism 101 (lecture series)
author: Kim Riddlebarger
summary: An introductory audio course on Reformed amillennialism given at Christ Reformed Church, including sessions on the definition of amillennialism and on covenant theology and eschatology.
note: Confirmed via search index (Monergism listing); audio not reviewed directly.

title: The Time Is at Hand
author: Jay E. Adams
summary: A short study of Revelation from a largely preterist angle that proposes 'realized millennialism' as a better name than 'amillennialism' for the view that the millennium is the present age.
note: Bibliographic details confirmed only through reviews and library catalogues (first published 1966; P&R edition 1974). Reviewers differ on whether to class Adams as amil or postmil.

title: Regnum Caelorum: Patterns of Millennial Thought in Early Christianity (2nd ed.)
author: Charles E. Hill
summary: Argues that non-chiliastic eschatology, tied to belief that the souls of the faithful go at once to heaven, was more widespread in the early church than often assumed.

title: The End Times Made Simple
author: Samuel E. Waldron
summary: A brief Reformed Baptist case for amillennialism built around the 'one coming, one resurrection, one judgment' structure of New Testament eschatology.

title: Thy Kingdom Come: Studies in Daniel and Revelation
author: R. J. Rushdoony
summary: Rushdoony's postmillennial reading of Daniel and Revelation, foundational for the Christian Reconstruction movement's eschatology of dominion.

title: The Presence of the Future: The Eschatology of Biblical Realism
author: George Eldon Ladd
summary: Ladd's influential account of the kingdom of God as both present ('already') in Jesus' ministry and future ('not yet'), the basis for his inaugurated historic premillennialism.

title: The Church and the Tribulation
author: Robert H. Gundry
summary: A detailed exegetical case for a posttribulational rapture, arguing that the church is preserved through, not removed before, the tribulation.

title: The Rapture: Pre-, Mid-, or Post-Tribulational?
author: Richard R. Reiter, Paul D. Feinberg, Gleason L. Archer, Douglas J. Moo
summary: Multi-view volume: Feinberg defends pretribulationism, Archer a mid-seventieth-week rapture, and Moo posttribulationism, each with responses.

title: Antichrist Before the Day of the Lord: What Every Christian Needs to Know about the Return of Christ
author: Alan E. Kurschner
summary: A popular-level defence of the prewrath view: the church meets the Antichrist's great tribulation, which is cut short by Christ's coming to rescue his people before the Day of the Lord's wrath. Prewrath is futurist and premillennial but not necessarily dispensational.
note: Kurschner directs Eschatos Ministries; title confirmed via booksellers' listings only.

title: The Case for Progressive Dispensationalism: The Interface Between Dispensational and Non-Dispensational Theology
author: Robert L. Saucy
summary: Saucy's presentation of progressive dispensationalism, stressing the unity of God's kingdom program while keeping a distinct future for national Israel.

title: What Is Progressive Dispensationalism?
author: Thomas Ice
summary: A traditional (revised) dispensationalist's description and critique of progressive dispensationalism, from the Pre-Trib Research Center.
note: Existence confirmed via search index; page not fetched directly.

title: Developing Dispensationalism, Parts 1 and 2 (Bibliotheca Sacra 145)
author: Craig A. Blaising
summary: Two articles tracing dispensationalism's development from classical through revised forms and arguing for further development, a seedbed of progressive dispensationalism.
note: Citation (Bibliotheca Sacra 145:133–40 and 254–80) taken from secondary bibliographies.

title: The Scofield Reference Bible
author: C. I. Scofield (ed.)
summary: Annotated KJV whose notes spread classic dispensationalism (seven dispensations, Israel/church distinction, pretribulational rapture) across English-speaking evangelicalism; revised 1917 and 1967.

title: Has the Church Replaced Israel? A Theological Evaluation
author: Michael J. Vlach
summary: Defines and traces the history of supersessionism, evaluates its hermeneutics and proof-texts, and argues for national Israel's continuing theological significance.
note: Publisher page confirmed via search index.

title: Progressive Covenantalism: Charting a Course between Dispensational and Covenantal Theologies
author: Stephen J. Wellum and Brent E. Parker (eds.)
summary: Essays developing the Kingdom through Covenant approach, including Parker's chapter arguing that Christ typologically fulfils Israel and the church is the new covenant people in him.
note: Publisher page confirmed via search index.

title: Kingdom through Covenant: A (Dispensational) Review
author: Detroit Baptist Theological Seminary (blog)
summary: A dispensational assessment of Gentry and Wellum's 'third way', appreciating its covenant storyline while questioning its handling of ethnic Israel's future role.
note: Existence confirmed via search index; author name not captured.

title: Covenant and God's Purpose for the World
author: Thomas R. Schreiner
summary: A short biblical theology of the covenants from creation to the new covenant, broadly aligned with progressive covenantalism.

title: The Church and Israel: The Issue
author: Ligonier Ministries (Tabletalk)
summary: Argues that the Reformed view of one people of God sees the gospel as fulfilling, not replacing, the older covenant economy, and distinguishes this from 'extreme replacement theology'.
note: Existence and argument confirmed via search index; page not fetched directly.

title: Is Covenant Theology the Same as Replacement Theology?
author: Monergism
summary: A Reformed Q&A rejecting the 'replacement theology' label for covenant theology and pointing to essays by Storms, Riddlebarger and R. Scott Clark.
note: Confirmed via search index; page not fetched directly.

title: The Israel of God: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow
author: O. Palmer Robertson
summary: A covenant-theological study of land, temple, and 'all Israel' in Romans 11, arguing that the promises reach their goal in Christ and the one people of God.

title: Introducing Covenant Theology (originally God of Promise)
author: Michael S. Horton
summary: An accessible introduction to the covenants of redemption, works, and grace and their bearing on Israel, church, and sacraments.

title: The Economy of the Covenants Between God and Man
author: Herman Witsius
summary: A classic systematic statement of Reformed federal theology, seeking to reconcile Cocceian and Voetian emphases.
